title: Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements
summary: What the system does vs how well/safe/fast/operable it must be.
explain: Functional requirements describe capabilities (view orders, approve discount). Non-functional requirements (NFRs) constrain quality: security, privacy, latency, availability, cost, accessibility, auditability. Stakeholders often propose solutions ('use Kafka') as if they were requirements — separate ends from means.
analogy: Functional: 'cross the river'. NFR: 'in under 5 minutes, safely, under $10'.
whyItMatters: Architecture fails when NFRs are discovered in production incidents.
mnemonic: NAME IT TO TAME IT: Say “Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements” + one failure mode out loud — if you can't, you don't own it yet. (Functional → mechanism → failure)
useCases: Greenfield design workshop: decide if “Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements” is required given constraints (latency, clean-core, team skills).
Incident bridge: symptoms appear; use “Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements” to classify the failing hop before changing config.
Architecture review board: defend why you accepted residual risk around “Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements”.
